items.title: HSREB approves the updated study protocol and Letter of Information
items.description: Western's Health Sciences Research Ethics Board approved the amended Study Protocol (Version 5) and the device-use Letter of Information and Consent (Version 3) on 13 Oct 2026. The protocol now lists all 26 partner locations and the Drug Analysis Service referral pathway. The V3 letter is available under Documents and replaces the previous version for all new participants.

items.title: Three organizations join the network
items.description: LOFT Community Services (mobile drug checking in York Region) signed its site agreement on 12 Aug 2026 and holds a mobile exemption valid to 30 Sep 2027. Agreements with CMHA Huron Perth Addiction and Mental Health Services (Stratford) and BRAS Outaouais (Gatineau) are executed, with device installation and training planned for December 2026.

items.title: Exemption decisions received over the summer
items.description: Positive Living Niagara was granted two mobile drug-checking exemptions on 17 Jul 2026 (valid to 31 Jul 2027). County of Grey holds renewed fixed, mobile and outreach-truck exemptions valid to 31 Jul 2027. Boyle Street Community Services received its exemption decision on 2 Sep 2026. LOFT Community Services holds a mobile exemption valid to 30 Sep 2027. Please keep sending Cameron copies of decision letters as they arrive.

items.title: Western laboratory confirmation testing paused
items.description: Western's mass spectrometry confirmation service has been paused since July 2026 while the laboratory analyst position is recruited. Sites with samples that need confirmatory analysis should contact Cameron about referral options in the meantime.

items.title: Drug-Checking Peer training held at AIDS New Brunswick
items.description: A Drug-Checking Peer training session was held at AIDS New Brunswick in Fredericton on 31 Jul 2026 with five attendees.

items.title: Moyo Health resumes drug checking
items.description: Moyo Health & Community Services resumed drug-checking services in Brampton on 20 Jul 2026 under the exemption issued 30 Jan 2026 (valid to 31 Jan 2027).

items.title: Ontario CTS funding ended 13 June
items.description: Provincial funding for Ontario consumption and treatment services ended on 13 Jun 2026. Four partner sites were affected: Ottawa Inner City Health, Sandy Hill CHC, Positive Living Niagara and Regional HIV/AIDS Connection. Drug-checking exemptions issued under CDSA s.56(1) are a separate federal authority and were not changed by the provincial decision.

items.title: Prairie Harm Reduction leaves the network
items.description: Prairie Harm Reduction's exemption was suspended on 30 Mar 2026 and the Saskatoon site has since closed. The device was retrieved in June and reassigned within the network.

items.title: 📄 DCP Training Invoice Package Now Available
items.description: The Drug-Checking Peer (DCP) Training & Certification Invoice Submission Package is now available for download. East Coast and other upcoming training sites: please complete and return your invoice to Cameron at cbrown58@uwo.ca as soon as possible so that your $3,000 CAD stipend can be processed before month end. If your organization already has its own invoice format, feel free to use that — the package is provided as a guide for sites that need one.

items.title: ⚠️ Ontario CTS Funding Cuts — Drug-Checking Services Context
items.description: On March 13, 2026, the Ontario Ministry of Health notified seven provincially-funded Consumption and Treatment Services (CTS) sites that provincial funding will terminate effective June 13, 2026. Five of our Ontario partner sites may be affected. Critically, the Province confirmed in court proceedings that drug-checking services are NOT captured by the CCRA — they are authorized under a separate federal CDSA Section 56(1) pathway and may be able to continue independently of supervised consumption services. Please read the full information document and contact Cameron directly with any questions.

items.title: ⚠️ Important Update: Ontario CTS Site Funding Announcement
items.description: On March 13, 2026, the Ontario Ministry of Health notified seven provincially-funded Consumption and Treatment Services (CTS) sites that provincial funding will terminate effective June 13, 2026. This announcement may affect certain Ontario project partner sites. Importantly, drug checking services are authorized under CDSA Section 56(1) — a separate federal pathway from supervised consumption. The Western University project team has prepared a detailed information document for affected partners outlining the regulatory landscape, your exemption status, and available options for continuing drug-checking services. Please contact Cameron directly with any questions.

items.title: 🚨 London Mass Overdose Event — Scatr Drug-Checking Plays Key Public Role
items.description: On March 11–12, 2026, London experienced a mass overdose emergency after a suspect drove through the downtown core distributing a toxic substance. Emergency services responded to 39 overdose-related calls in 24 hours and London hospitals activated a Code Orange Alert. Scatr drug-checking services at Carepoint (RHAC) played a direct public health role during the crisis. Lily Bialas, RHAC's Interim Director of Harm Reduction, was cited in CBC and CTV coverage highlighting the importance of on-site drug checking for providing timely, accurate information about drug supply trends — exactly what this network was built to do.

items.title: Exemption decisions for Cochrane and AIDS New Brunswick
items.description: Cochrane District Paramedic Service received its mobile exemption decision on 6 Mar 2026 (valid to 31 Mar 2027) and AIDS New Brunswick received its exemption on 10 Mar 2026.

items.title: 🎉 Paper Published in Harm Reduction Journal!
items.description: Our peer-reviewed manuscript has been published as open access in Harm Reduction Journal (Springer Nature). The paper — "Street drug monitoring with networked spectrometers powered by machine learning: a pilot study in Ontario, Canada" — reports on 7,752 samples analyzed across 10 Ontario sites over 14 months, comparing Raman spectroscopy against HPLC-MS and documenting participant consumption-related behavior changes. Congratulations to all co-authors and partner sites whose participation made this research possible!

items.title: New Resource: Standard Operating Procedures for Sample Preparation
items.description: We have published the official Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for Sample Preparation document. This resource outlines the proper protocols for packaging and labelling samples for transport to the Western Laboratory. All partner sites are reminded to review and adhere to these SOPs to ensure sample integrity, regulatory compliance, and accurate analysis results.

items.title: Reminder: Sample Submission Accountability
items.description: Health Canada requires every sample to be accounted for. Please only use the sample submission feature in the Scatr portal when there is a real sample to submit. Accurate record-keeping is essential for regulatory compliance and the integrity of our network data.

items.title: Health Canada Releases Updated National Opioid & Stimulant Harms Data
items.description: The Public Health Agency of Canada has published updated national surveillance data showing a 17% decrease in opioid toxicity deaths in 2024 compared to 2023. Key findings: deaths dropped from 8,623 (2023) to 7,146 (2024), averaging 20 deaths per day (down from 22). Hospitalizations also fell 15%, alongside similar decreases in EMS responses and ED visits. BC, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, and Yukon all reported decreases, with some jurisdictions attributing the decline partly to lower fentanyl concentrations in the drug supply.

items.title: Share Your Story: PWLLE Voices Needed
items.description: At the heart of this project is a simple belief: the best improvements to drug-checking services come directly from the people who use them. We want to hear from People with Lived or Living Experience (PWLLEs) who are willing to share their stories and perspectives. Your insights help shape how these services evolve. Interested in having a conversation? Contact Cameron at cbrown58@uwo.ca — no pressure, just a chance to be heard.
